Keys IV antibiotics as "standard initial management" for mild preseptal cellulitis in a well child; oral antibiotics are usual, IV for systemic upset or no improvement. No oral option offered. Contradicts #7 in the same set.
Stem gives no infective signs (fever, erythema, warmth); post-traumatic subcutaneous emphysema (option B) is at least as likely. The explanation itself says to tell them apart by those signs.
Keys "pseudogout" as the right label per G-CAN. The international terminology consensus, as I understand it, advises "acute CPP crystal arthritis" instead. Verify against the source.
Keys "1-5%" for crowned dens syndrome among CPPD. Explanation admits "specific percentages can vary"; reference is "implied". No source for the figure.
Keys "CPPD with chronic arthropathy" as a G-CAN standardised label. That is not a recognised term (consensus uses terms such as "chronic CPP crystal inflammatory arthritis").
The "may not increase weight by 36 weeks postmenstrual age" finding concerns preterm infants; the stem is a term 2-month-old with a severely malnourished mother, where supplementation is indicated.
Stem ends with the case and never asks a question. Answer (step-up drainage for infected necrosis) is correct.
Stem ends with the case and never asks a question. Key (percutaneous drainage) is acceptable.

Keys losartan-induced pancreatitis as "most likely" in a man with epigastric pain radiating to the back and no gallstones on ultrasound (which misses microlithiasis). Gallstone or alcohol aetiology is far more likely. Also misfiled under necrotising pancreatitis.

Tonsillectomy at 4 episodes/12 months does not meet the usual thresholds (Paradise/SIGN/NICE). Key overclaims "complete symptom elimination" and cites a "WHO 2025 guideline G6" that is not a known WHO tonsillectomy guideline.

Reduced processing speed is not a criterion separating early MS from RIS. Stem already has visual symptoms, so RIS (no symptoms) does not apply. Diagnosis rests on a clinical attack or DIS/DIT (McDonald 2017).
Multiple hepatic masses in a 45-year-old: HCC or metastases must be excluded first; keying tuberculous granuloma as "most crucial" risks anchoring. Misfiled under TB screening.
Gestational sac with yolk sac but no fetal pole is a pregnancy of uncertain viability: NICE advises repeat scan at least 7 days later, not serial hCG with repeat scan at 48-72 hours.
In AF with RVR and COPD, diltiazem (A) is usually preferred over a beta-blocker; guidance recommends non-dihydropyridine CCBs in COPD. Key C is defensible only with caution.

Keys sputum culture and Gram stain as the "most critical step before antibiotics" for CAP. Guidelines (ATS/IDSA) do not advise routine sputum culture for non-severe CAP, and antibiotics should not wait for it.
Applies the 4 cm observation threshold for renal angiomyolipoma (from a Czech journal) to a 3.5 cm solitary lung nodule. A >8 mm nodule needs PET-CT, biopsy or resection planning.

Keys leukapheresis as the initial step for AML hyperleukocytosis. It is contested and not routine; cytoreduction (hydroxyurea or induction) with hydration is standard. Reference admits "general knowledge, not from the provided articles".

After a single IM epinephrine dose, next step is repeat IM epinephrine and IV fluids, then IV epinephrine infusion. Keyed norepinephrine skips these steps.

Attributes "repositioning at least every 2 hours" to NICE. NICE CG179 advises 6-hourly for at-risk adults and 4-hourly for high risk, individualised to skin assessment. Keyed interval does not match the cited guideline.

Claims MRA plus SGLT2 inhibitor is the preferred dual-agent approach for albuminuric CKD. Guidelines build on RAS blockade plus SGLT2 inhibitor, adding finerenone for diabetes; the keyed statement of superiority is unsupported.

Claims eosinophilia >1500 is the hallmark of DRESS. RegiSCAR requires eosinophilia only >=0.7 x 10^9/L (or >10%); liver involvement is the most common organ finding. Key too specific and partly wrong.
Implies phenytoin may be safe after carbamazepine DRESS. Aromatic anticonvulsants cross-react often and standard advice is to avoid all of them; keyed option C is hazardous.
Keys "no specific treatment" for recurrent membranous nephropathy in allografts, citing 2002 guidance. Rituximab and other immunotherapy are now used; keyed answer outdated.

Keys ECG for routine noninvasive rejection surveillance after heart transplant. Standard is endomyocardial biopsy, gene-expression profiling or donor-derived cfDNA; ECG is not reliable. Also misfiled under renal transplant recurrence.

Keys St John's Wort as best-evidenced herbal remedy for anxiety. Evidence is for mild-moderate depression; it has major drug interactions and is not recommended for anxiety. Unsafe teaching.

Key is "retrospective data suggest varying conclusions"; non-answer, no clinical decision.

CURB-65 miscalculated: RR is 28 (<30), urea not given; stated score 4 is wrong. Score is about 3; ICU decision is not made on CURB-65 alone.
Claims a minimum of 48 hours IV before oral switch for severe CAP. Guidelines base switch on clinical stability, not a fixed duration; attributed to ATS 2019 incorrectly.

Key rests on COVID-19 troponin data applied to bacterial CAP; the cited paper is not about CAP.

Gram-positive cocci in clusters in a ventilated severe CAP patient is a common trigger to cover MRSA pending cultures; keyed "do not add" is contestable.

Keys piperacillin-tazobactam plus vancomycin for a nursing-home resident with severe CAP. ATS/IDSA 2019 dropped HCAP; empiric beta-lactam plus macrolide (option A) remains standard unless specific MRSA/Pseudomonas risk factors exist.

An asymptomatic TB-exposed patient on infliximab does not require a negative-pressure room; guidance is to avoid co-locating immunosuppressed patients with infectious TB patients and to screen for latent TB. Keyed isolation is overkill.
Before adalimumab, TB screening and HBV serology are most crucial; keyed HCV-only screening is the least important of the required tests.

Positive IGRA with healed granuloma: treat latent TB (rifampicin or isoniazid) before biologic. Option E is also correct; keyed referral only is incomplete. Explanation admits it is not supported by guidelines.
Repeating TST/IGRA after treated LTBI is not useful (tests stay positive). Correct step is symptom/CXR review to exclude active TB, not repeat screening.
Key borrows a NICE abortion-services HIV test recommendation for biologic pre-screening; guidance does not state this. Low value and misattributed.
Asks which general infection-prevention measure is "NOT recommended" (antibiotic locks); unrelated to biologic screening.
Asks which measure is "inconsistent" with NICE (in-line filters); unrelated to biologic screening.
Keys low-dose trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole prophylaxis even though the isolate is resistant to it; and postmenopausal vaginal estrogen is the guideline-preferred first step (option C).

Keys DECT of sacroiliac joints for suspected axial gout; axial gout is rare and MRI is the standard test for acute sacroiliac pain. Key rests on a single review mention.
Asks for a creatinine threshold for pyrazinamide dosing; explanation admits it is not from guidelines. Dosing adjusts by creatinine clearance.
Keys R-GDP immunochemotherapy as NICE salvage for MDR-TB; R-GDP is a lymphoma regimen. Factually wrong.

Keys stopping both aspirin and ticagrelor before CABG. Aspirin should be continued; ticagrelor stopped about 3 days before surgery.

With AF and OAC, clopidogrel is preferred; switching to prasugrel/ticagrelor for CYP2C19 poor metabolisers is not guideline-supported and raises bleeding.

Keys baseline PFTs/DLCO as the most critical assessment before an ADC; guidelines require LVEF for trastuzumab deruxtecan and monitoring for ILD, not mandatory baseline PFTs. Cited source is a gynaecologic oncology society statement.
NICE has no recommendation for vitamin A supplementation in paediatric pneumonia; WHO/Cochrane show no benefit. Fabricated guideline claim.
Post-transplant child with prolonged fever and cough: invasive fungal infection and CMV/respiratory viruses are far more likely than TB; keyed TB is not supported.
